speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; could you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they have been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of walking unsteadily and feeling clumsy, particularly on your right side, suggest a problem in your brain or spinal cord. To help narrow this down, have you experienced any recent changes in your vision, such as double vision or blurred sight?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, the sudden onset of ataxia and clumsiness strongly suggests PML, a serious brain infection caused by the JC virus. I need to confirm the extent of this with imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI_with_contrast.
